title: A user's Permission Sets tab shows API names: permission-ref / position-ref cells have no label read face (#27521 row 14)
body:
domain:ui#2 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CY2n1JmZZKrHgtp9jC

Filing gate: ② a wrong or confusing state shown to the user. Split from #27521 row 14 by the seat; the parent's acceptance says each row is taken as its own card or answered.

## Business reason

Who: every administrator opening a user. What happens: the user's Permission Sets related list shows `organization_admin_no_bypass` / `admin_full_access` instead of the sets' labels, so the administrator cannot tell what a user holds without opening each set. Reach: every administrator opening a user; the same holds for Positions.

## Mechanism

- `sys_user_permission_set.permission_set` (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/sys-user-permission-set.object.ts`) is a by-name text column with `widget: 'permission-ref'`; `sys_user_position.position` likewise declares `widget: 'position-ref'`.
- On main the widget is honoured on the edit face only (the picker in `ui/packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx`); no `@object-ui/fields` list or detail cell reads the registry label, so the cell draws the stored name.

Measured at `main` @ `561b7642`, re-driven (stock `examples/app-showcase --seed-admin`, admin, Chromium 1440×900).

## Wanted

A read face in `@object-ui/fields` for `permission-ref` / `position-ref` cells that draws the registry label (from the catalog the picker already reads), with the API name on `title`, falling back to the name when the catalog has no entry.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A user's Permission Sets tab shows each set's label; hovering shows the API name.
- [ ] The Positions tab does the same for `position-ref`.
- [ ] A name the catalog does not know still renders (the name itself), with a test pinning the fallback.

Refs #27521
